newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares end lower as results bring gloom.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares end lower as results bring gloom.

text.p: Bombay shares ended lower on Wednesday as key results from index-linked stocks disappointed the market, traders said.
Bombay's benchmark index closed 4.15 points, or 0.11 percent, lower at a provisional 3688.40.
Steelmaker SAIL said its net profit plunged to 5.27 billion rupees for the year ended March 31, from 13.19 billion in the previous year.
Multinational Colgate-Palmolive (India) said its 1996/97 net rose marginally to 780.3 million rupees, from 775.8 million.
"The results were disastrous," said a trader at a foreign brokerage.
Shares of truckmaker Tata Engineering & Locomotive Company (TELCO) erased most early gains as speculators booked profits at higher levels, traders said.
TELCO shares ended 2.25 rupees higher at 395.25 -- off an early high of 408.25 hit minutes after opening on hectic bids after its results beat expectations.
TELCO said late on Tuesday its net profit jumped 44 percent to 7.62 billion rupees in the year ended March 31, from 5.3 billion in the previous year.
Automobile analysts -- who had pegged their 1996/97 net profit forecasts at around 7.2 billion rupees -- said a lower taxation rate and improved operating margins boosted profits.
TELCO's effective rate of tax was 24 percent in 1996/97, compared to 30 percent in the previous year.
After the initial results euphoria faded, investors would look towards an impending hike in diesel prices that was bound to bring the stock lower, analysts said.
Shares of Mahanagar Telephone Nigam Ltd climbed 6.50 rupees, or 2.3 percent, to 283.50 ahead of the firm's results due later today, traders said.
Analysts said MTNL is expected to report a jump in net profit to 8.6 billion rupees in 1996/97, up 18 percent from 7.29 billion in the previous year. Results are also due from leading refiner BPCL.
Larsen & Toubro and Siemens shares fell ahead of results announcements later this week, traders said.
Petrochemicals firm IPCL continued to head lower after the firm's said on Monday its 1996/97 net fell to 5.10 billion rupees, from 6.04 billion in the previous year.
